series: trendwatching.com annual consumer trends (free Trend Briefing)
title: 10 CRUCIAL CONSUMER TRENDS FOR 2010
notes: Labelled the December 2009 Trend Briefing; first archived 2009-11-18, so published by then. Labels are the numbered heading images' alt text; item 11 'NEED MORE?' is a promotion for the paid Premium service and is not a trend. target_year 2010 from the title. The 100+ page 2010 Trend Report (Premium) is not captured.

entries.label: BUSINESS AS UNUSUAL
entries.quote: For the first time, there’s a global understanding, if not a feeling of urgency that sustainability, in every possible meaning of the word, is the only way forward.
entries.subject: Sustainability as a business imperative
entries.note: Preceded by 'In 2010, prepare for 'business as unusual'.'

entries.label: URBANY
entries.quote: A defining trend for 2010, 2011, 2012, and so on: urbanization on steroids.
entries.subject: Urbanization and urban consumers
entries.note: Section quotes a third-party figure: urban share of world population exceeded 50 per cent in 2008 (past, not a forecast).

entries.label: REAL-TIME REVIEWS
entries.quote: let’s dive into one sub-trend that will be truly disruptive: the rise of REAL-TIME REVIEWS.
entries.subject: Real-time consumer reviews

entries.label: (F)LUXURY
entries.quote: In 2010, luxury, and what it means to a bewildering number of ‘consumer segments’, will remain in flux.
entries.subject: Shifting definitions of luxury

entries.label: MASS MINGLING
entries.quote: More people than ever will be living large parts of their lives online in 2010. Yet, those same people will also mingle, meet up, and congregate more often with other ‘warm bodies’ in the offline world .
entries.subject: Offline meetups enabled by social and mobile media
entries.note: Source has a space before the final full stop.

entries.label: ECO-EASY
entries.quote: serious eco-results will depend on making products and processes more sustainable without consumers even noticing it
entries.subject: Default sustainability built into products and processes
entries.note: Quote is the first clause of a longer sentence.

entries.label: TRACKING & ALERTING
entries.quote: If INFOLUST (consumers lusting after relevant information) is the enduring mega trend, then TRACKING and ALERTING are its du jour sub-trends.
entries.subject: Consumer tracking and alert services

entries.label: EMBEDDED GENEROSITY
entries.quote: It incorporates all giving initiatives that make giving and donating painless, if not automatic
entries.subject: Painless, automatic giving and donating
entries.note: 'It' is EMBEDDED GENEROSITY; the text says GENERATION G 'will be even bigger in 2010'.

entries.label: PROFILE MYNING
entries.quote: we're putting our money on data and profile mining by its rightful owners , i.e. consumers.
entries.subject: Consumers monetizing their own personal data
entries.note: Source has a space before the comma.

entries.label: MATURIALISM
entries.quote: Let’s face it: 2010 will be rawer, more opinionated, more risqué, more in your face than ever before.
entries.subject: Risqué, mature consumer culture
entries.note: Recycled label: MATURIALISM was a 2004 monthly briefing.
